LHX.sentence: L3Harris barely budged today, and while it's the smallest of the big defense contractors and earns thinner profits than its rivals, steady military spending keeps the business on solid footing.

ASML.sentence: ASML slipped a bit, but this is the only company in the world that makes a certain kind of chipmaking machine, and the recent price looks steep mostly because last year's earnings were unusually low.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly steady — the world's biggest industrial gas supplier is unusually priced right in line with a smaller rival rather than at its usual premium, which is odd for a company this well-run.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — its stock has already bounced back strongly while the rest of its group lagged, so the exciting cloud-and-AI story keeps chugging along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is holding steady, and there's a hopeful sign underneath: biotech funding is thawing, which usually means more lab-equipment orders for them a couple of quarters down the road.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge ticked up a little — this pipeline operator works like a toll road for oil and gas and pays a nice dividend, though it isn't especially cheap at the moment.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow rose today and has fallen unusually far from its high for such a reliable business — corporations and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI automation tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped slightly, but its commodity-trading arm is holding up better than copper prices alone would suggest, which is exactly the diversification this miner-plus-trader is supposed to offer.

RDDT.sentence: Reddit dropped again on the worry that Google could send it fewer visitors, but its advertising revenue is actually growing very fast, so the fear is running ahead of the business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA edged up — Latin America's biggest Coke bottler looks inexpensive and pays a steadily growing dividend, a quiet and dependable holding.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is flat, and while its profits look strong right now, that's partly because oil prices are high — which means earnings may be near a peak rather than a bargain.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk pulled back today after a big run-up — this Danish container-shipping giant had climbed unusually far above its recent trend, and shipping is a boom-and-bust business, so some cooling off isn't surprising.

MA.sentence: Mastercard climbed today and is quietly priced a touch below its twin Visa, even though it's growing a little faster — people keep tapping their cards all over the world.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot maker was flat today but has fallen while other medical-device stocks rose — it looks like nervousness about this one company specifically rather than anything wrong with its business, which keeps earning more each time a hospital uses a da Vinci robot.
